s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, severe, mechanical low back pain and mental depression with cutaneous and subcutaneous lesions and muscle contractures
salient_findings: Large and deep, irregularly shaped, cutaneous ulcer on the right forearm
Woody induration of skin on forearms and abdominal region
Bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles
key_facts: 7-year history of severe, mechanical, low back pain
Long-standing mental depression
Current medications include duloxetine hydrochloride, clonazepam, oxcarbazepine, fentanyl, sulpiride, zopiclone, omeprazole magnesium, and baclofen
Self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, 100 mg 4 times per day, for the past 3 years
Elevated serum creatinine kinase (192 U/L)
Normal complete blood cell count
Normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Normal antinuclear antibody
Normal rheumatoid factor
Histopathology shows lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates
Severe fibrosis in deep dermis and subcutaneous septa
Foreign-body giant cells and macrophages with large, foamy cytoplasm present

shortlist.label: Factitial panniculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine and presence of lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates

shortlist.label: Lipodermatosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of woody induration of skin on both forearms and abdominal region, and severe fibrosis in deep dermis and subcutaneous septa

shortlist.label: Panniculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology shows lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates

shortlist.label: Meperidine-induced skin and muscle lesions
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine and presence of cutaneous and subcutaneous lesions

shortlist.label: Weber-Christian disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of lobular panniculitis and severe fibrosis in deep dermis and subcutaneous septa, which are characteristic of this disease

raw.rationale: The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, 100 mg 4 times per day, for the past 3 years, correlates with the development of skin and muscle lesions, including large and deep cutaneous ulcers, woody induration of skin, and muscle contractures, which are consistent with meperidine-induced lesions.

rejected.label: Factitial panniculitis
rejected.why: While the patient's self-injection of meperidine could be considered factitious behavior, the specific diagnosis of factitial panniculitis does not fully capture the extent of the patient's lesions and muscle involvement.

rejected.label: Lipodermatosclerosis
rejected.why: Lipodermatosclerosis typically presents with pain, swelling, and induration of the lower legs, which does not match the patient's presentation of lesions on the forearms and abdominal region.

rejected.label: Panniculitis
rejected.why: Panniculitis is a broader term that encompasses various forms of inflammation of the subcutaneous fat, but it does not specifically account for the patient's history of meperidine injections and the resulting lesions.

rejected.label: Weber-Christian disease
rejected.why: Weber-Christian disease is a rare form of panniculitis characterized by recurrent, painful nodules, but it does not typically involve the extensive skin and muscle lesions seen in this patient, nor is it associated with meperidine use.
